correctness.rationale: For fixed b>=2 and epsilon=tau/sqrt(n), the small C^0 conjugacy H_epsilon to the linear degree-b map is obtained by a contraction of the inverse-expanding cohomological equation and expanded uniformly to third order in epsilon. Along its periodic points the log-derivative sum has epsilon S_n g+epsilon² S_n h+O_b(n|epsilon|³), with g=(2pi/b)cos(2pi x), Haar mean h=pi²/b², and g’s long-run variance 2pi²/b². Sampling fixed points is within O(b^-n) total variation of uniform cyclic base-b words; digit-block truncation and Lindeberg prove S_n g/sqrt(n) Gaussian, while LLN gives S_n h/n -> pi²/b². Thus the triangular array tends to N(pi²tau²/b²,2pi²tau²/b²), tau=0 degenerate. Finite-period discrete Fourier orthogonality for n>=3 gives exact zero first derivative, variance 2npi²/b², curvature (2npi²/b²)(b^n+1)/(b^n-1). Independent root-of-unity calculations verified Fourier covariance for b=2..6, n=3..8 and curvature for b=2..5, n=3..7; those are not a CLT proof.
